correctness.rationale: For every integer \(r\ge3\), positive differences in \(U_r=\{2^j-1:0\le j<r\}\) have unique \(2\)-adic valuations and odd quotients, so every nonzero difference occurs once. Scaling by \(2^r\) preserves uniqueness and separates the two difference sets except at zero; this also makes cross sums unique. Therefore the prescribed adjacency coefficients are all 0 or 1, with no loops or multiple edges. The \(A\)-backbone contains displacement 1, and \(A_n\) and \(B_n\) have a zero-displacement edge, so the graph is connected. The full Floquet matrix obeys the exact rank-one identity \(H_r(z)+rI=[u_r(z),v_r(z^{-1})]^T[u_r(z^{-1}),v_r(z)]\), proving the eigenvalue \(-r\) exists at every quasimomentum and is spectral bottom. A nonzero finite Laurent kernel vector gives an actual finite-support eigenfunction; translations imply infinite multiplicity. The other fiber eigenvalue is nonconstant because \(|u_r(z)|<r\) when \(z\ne1\), so the flat band is unique. The exact checker verified both Laurent coefficients and real-space recurrences through \(r=8\); the analytic proof establishes all \(r\), with no inference from finite samples.

originality.rationale: Section 5.2 of Sabri and Youssef (arXiv:2304.06465, 2023) directly asks whether two-orbit zero-potential unit-weight periodic adjacency operators have flat-band energies other than \(0,-1,-2\). The new theorem constructs, for every \(r\ge3\), a connected two-orbit simple unweighted graph with a flat band at \(-r\), thereby answering this precise open existence question. Their general generator from finite graphs increases the orbit count, and their necessary two-orbit coefficient identities do not imply construction of any additional energy. Faust--Kachkovskiy arXiv:2509.01927 Theorem 1.4 concerns generic onsite potentials and does not imply absence or presence at the exceptional zero potential. Alternate weighted or multi-band model constructions do not enforce the zero-one graph conditions. Targeted literature searches and statement-level comparisons identified no prior theorem entailing the two-orbit integer family.
residual_risks: A weakly indexed equivalent example could exist under long-range two-band tight-binding or cyclic-voltage-graph terminology despite targeted searches.

value.rationale: Sabri--Youssef (2023), Section 5.2, explicitly identify the possible flat-band energies for connected simple unweighted two-orbit graphs as an open existence problem beyond 0, -1 and -2. This construction provides an infinite parametric answer, showing every negative integer from \(-3\) downward occurs despite the two-site motif. Its use of additive unique-difference sets simultaneously satisfies zero-one hopping constraints, connectivity, and exact spectral factorization. The result is structurally motivated by a stated research gap, and the unbounded energy family plus explicit eigenfunctions is not a routine numerical increment. Long-range/degree growth and incompleteness for positive energies are stated limitations.
